subject: English Literature
qualification: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE (9-1) in English Literature
specVersion: Specification Issue 3, August 2025 (first teaching September 2016; first examination June 2018)
statusNote: Code, component structure, durations, marks, weightings, AOs and every text list were read from the Pearson 4ET1 specification PDF (Issue 3, August 2025) via a fetch tool that returns summaries, and the 4ET1/01 June 2025 examiners' report was read for question styles. Not read first-hand in full: the PDF in its entirety, the anthology itself, command-word and grade-descriptor sections, and mark schemes. Year and term placement is a recommended sequence. Replaces the earlier AQA 8702 file; the school's lesson files are still AQA 8702 based.

sources.title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Literature (2016) qualification page
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Literature 4ET1 specification (Issue 3)

tiers: None (single tier, graded 9 to 1; individual components are not graded)

assessment.title: Poetry and Modern Prose
assessment.content: Section A unseen poetry; Section B anthology poetry (16 poems); Section C modern prose (one text).
assessment.format: Externally assessed, closed book (clean anthology copy supplied). A: one 20-mark essay (AO2). B: one 30-mark question from two (AO2, AO3). C: one 40-mark question from two (AO1, AO4). Available June and November.

assessment.title: Modern Drama and Literary Heritage Texts
assessment.content: Section A modern drama; Section B literary heritage text.
assessment.format: Externally assessed, open book. A: one 30-mark question from two (AO1, AO2). B: one 30-mark question from two (AO1, AO2, AO4). Taken instead of Component 3.

assessment.title: Modern Drama and Literary Heritage Texts (coursework)
assessment.content: Assignment A modern drama; Assignment B literary heritage text.
assessment.format: Internally assessed, externally moderated. A: 30 marks (15 AO1, 15 AO2). B: 30 marks (10 AO1, 10 AO2, 10 AO4). Alternative to Component 2.

nonExam: Component 3 is an optional non-examined coursework route (two assignments, 60 marks, 40%), internally assessed and externally moderated, taken instead of Component 2. Candidates take Component 1 plus either Component 2 or Component 3. Linear: all assessment at the end of the course. Whether TGA would run Component 2 or 3 is not decided.

aos.desc: Show close knowledge of texts, with a critical style and informed personal engagement.
Analyse the writer's language, form and structure and the meanings and effects they create.
Explore links and connections between texts.
Show understanding of relationships between texts and the contexts in which they were written.

units.title: Component 1 Section A: Unseen poetry
points: One 20-mark essay question on a poem not seen before, assessed for AO2.
Candidates also study a selection of modern poetry to prepare for it.
Focus is language, form and structure and the effects they create.
Closed-book paper, so no prepared quotations are possible for this section.

units.title: Component 1 Section B: Anthology poetry (16 poems)
points: Part 3 of the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Anthology; all 16 poems are studied.
One 30-mark question from a choice of two, assessed for AO2 and AO3.
Questions ask candidates to compare poems; a clean copy of the poems is supplied.
Poems come from different periods and cultures, so links and connections between texts are credited.

units.title: Anthology poems 1 to 8
points: If- (Rudyard Kipling).
Prayer Before Birth (Louis MacNeice).
Blessing (Imtiaz Dharker).
Search For My Tongue (Sujata Bhatt).
Half-past Two (U A Fanthorpe).
Piano (D H Lawrence).
Hide and Seek (Vernon Scannell).
Sonnet 116: Let me not to the marriage of true minds (William Shakespeare).

units.title: Anthology poems 9 to 16
points: La Belle Dame sans Merci (John Keats).
Poem at Thirty-Nine (Alice Walker).
War Photographer (Carol Ann Duffy).
The Tyger (William Blake).
My Last Duchess (Robert Browning).
Half-caste (John Agard).
Do not go gentle into that good night (Dylan Thomas).
Remember (Christina Rossetti).

units.title: Component 1 Section C: Modern prose (choose one text)
points: One 40-mark question from a choice of two on the chosen prose text.
Assessed for AO1 (knowledge and personal engagement) and AO4 (context).
Closed book; the examiner report shows questions on theme, character and significance.
Context is credited where it relates to how the text was written and received.

units.title: Modern prose options listed by Pearson Edexcel
points: To Kill a Mockingbird (Harper Lee).
Of Mice and Men (John Steinbeck).
The Whale Rider (Witi Ihimaera).
The Joy Luck Club (Amy Tan).
Things Fall Apart (Chinua Achebe).
Klara and the Sun (Kazuo Ishiguro): new, first assessment May 2026.
Western Lane (Chetna Maroo): new, first assessment May 2026.

units.title: Component 2 or 3 Section A / Assignment A: Modern drama (choose one)
points: Component 2: one 30-mark question from a choice of two, open book, assessed for AO1 and AO2.
Component 3: internally assessed assignment of 30 marks (15 AO1, 15 AO2), externally moderated.
Drama is studied as a script for performance as well as a printed text.

units.title: Modern drama options listed by Pearson Edexcel
points: A View from the Bridge (Arthur Miller).
An Inspector Calls (J B Priestley).
The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-time (Mark Haddon, adapted by Simon Stephens).
Kindertransport (Diane Samuels).
Death and the King's Horseman (Wole Soyinka).

units.title: Component 2 or 3 Section B / Assignment B: Literary heritage texts (choose one)
points: Component 2: one 30-mark question from a choice of two, open book, assessed for AO1, AO2 and AO4.
Component 3: assignment of 30 marks (10 each for AO1, AO2 and AO4), internally assessed.
Non-examined marks from both assignments combine into one mark out of 60.
Candidates relate the text to the context in which it was written.

units.title: Literary heritage options listed by Pearson Edexcel
points: Romeo and Juliet (William Shakespeare).
Macbeth (William Shakespeare).
The Merchant of Venice (William Shakespeare).
Pride and Prejudice (Jane Austen).
Great Expectations (Charles Dickens).
The Scarlet Letter (Nathaniel Hawthorne).

units.title: SCHOOL CHOICE: Macbeth (literary heritage text)
points: Macbeth is on the Pearson Edexcel literary heritage list, so the school text is permitted.
Existing Y11 lessons teach it as context and witches, then tyranny, guilt and downfall.
Existing lessons are written to the AQA 8702 exam format and need re-mapping.
Open-book Component 2 allows the text to be used, so quotation recall matters less.
Marks differ: 30 marks on AO1, AO2 and AO4 rather than extract plus whole-text format.

units.title: SCHOOL CHOICE: A Christmas Carol (not on the Pearson list)
points: A Christmas Carol does not appear in the Pearson Edexcel 4ET1 text lists.
Existing Y10 lessons on it are AQA 8702 material and cannot be assessed here.
It could remain as wider reading on Victorian society and Dickens, not as a set text.
Closest Pearson option for Dickens: Great Expectations in the literary heritage list.

commandWords.meaning: Anthology Section B: set two poems side by side on ideas and methods (per 2025 report question wording).
Examine how a writer presents a theme, character or relationship; used in Section C and Component 2 stems (to be confirmed).

skills: Analysing language, form and structure in poems and prose.
Responding to an unseen poem without preparation.
Comparing two poems from different periods and cultures.
Writing an extended, personal and critical response to a modern prose text.
Using the text in the open-book drama or heritage response.
Relating a text to its context without bolting on facts.
Planning and timing: about 40 minutes on the anthology and 45 on prose (examiner guide).

prerequisites.from: KS3 poetry from different cultures and periods
Year 9 Of Mice and Men (if used)

links.topic: Language and structure analysis, extended writing
links.how: Language builds the analytical method; Literature applies it to poems and set texts.

links.topic: Pearson International GCSE English Language A (4EA1) uses poetry and prose texts
links.how: 4EA1 Components 2 and 3 also study anthology texts, so texts and teaching could be shared.

links.topic: Jacobean England: kingship, James I, the Gunpowder Plot
links.how: History explains beliefs about monarchy; Literature uses them as context for Macbeth.

links.topic: Great Depression and the 1930s American South
links.how: History gives background for Of Mice and Men and To Kill a Mockingbird.

links.topic: Britain in 1945 and class: An Inspector Calls
links.how: History supplies the period setting that Priestley's play criticises.

links.topic: Colonialism in Africa: Things Fall Apart
links.how: History explains the colonial and missionary context of Achebe's novel.

links.topic: Justice, mercy and moral responsibility as shared themes
links.how: Islamic Studies gives ethical vocabulary for discussion; Literature stays on the writers' methods.

links.topic: Poetic form, voice and identity in translation
links.how: Poems on language and identity (Search For My Tongue, Half-caste) invite comparison with Arabic poetry study.

links.topic: Place and environment in poetry and prose
links.how: Geography provides place knowledge; Literature analyses how settings are created.

links.topic: Visual imagery for Romantic and Victorian poems
links.how: Art analyses visual methods; Literature applies imagery to language.

contextNote: AO4 requires context to be taught accurately and linked to the writer's choices (for example colonial history in Things Fall Apart, or Jacobean kingship in Macbeth). Teach what the context was; keep discussion text-focused.
